page: Vultr vx1-m-32c-256gb is a memory-optimized cloud server instance belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, the configuration supplies 16 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 256.0 GB of RAM, offering a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per thread. The processor integrates 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2.

Hardware architecture excludes discrete GPU accelerators and bundles a minimal 1 GB NVMe SSD for local boot and system partitions, complemented by a single assigned public IPv4 address. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates upper-percentile execution capabilities. Geekbench testing reports single-core and multi-core scores in the top tier at 2,752.0 and 23,765.0 respectively. PassMark memory testing ranks in the top tier at 3,068.77, while uncached large-block memory writes reach 196.72 GB/sec. Data processing throughput reflects similar efficiency, with single-threaded gzip compression achieving 40.57 GB/sec and Redis key-value operations handling 63.76 million operations per second.

The primary operational tradeoff centers on disk capacity. With only 1 GB of local NVMe storage, data-intensive workloads require network-attached storage or external volume attachments to operate effectively. In exchange, the instance provides high compute density, dedicated CPU execution, and expansive memory capacity relative to its resource footprint. These attributes make the vx1-m-32c-256gb well suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including large in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, real-time analytics, compilation pipelines, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Vultr vx1-m-32c-256gb is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring a dedicated 32-vCPU, 16-physical-core AMD EPYC processor operating at 2.0 GHz, paired with 256.0 GB of system memory. Lacking hardware GPU acceleration and limited to 1 GB of local NVMe storage, the architecture focuses on memory density and CPU throughput. Supported CPU extensions include AVX-512 (VNNI and BF16), SHA-NI, and VAES. In synthetic and application benchmarks, it produces top-tier memory scores, reaching 196.72 GB/sec in large-block write operations, alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 23,765.0 and Redis throughput of 63.76 million SET operations per second. Because local storage is strictly minimal, external storage attachments are required for data persistence. This server type fits in-memory caching systems, large transactional or analytical databases, and intensive compute workloads requiring substantial RAM allocations.
